title: The oldest computer
text: In 1901, sponge divers exploring a Roman-era shipwreck off the Greek island of Antikythera brought up a corroded lump of bronze that nobody could {{1}}. Split open, it {{2}} gear wheels of astonishing precision, and for decades the fragment was filed away as an astronomical curiosity. It was, in fact, a geared calculator, built around 100 BC to {{3}} the positions of the sun and moon, predict eclipses and even track the four-year cycle of athletic games. Nothing of comparable mechanical sophistication is known from the next thousand years; geared mechanisms of this {{4}} reappear in Europe only with medieval clocks. The device overturns comfortable assumptions about the ancient world: precision engineering did not begin with the Renaissance but was a {{5}} tradition, waiting to be rediscovered, and the workshop skills behind the Antikythera mechanism were {{6}} — no manual and no training text survives. X-ray imaging has let researchers read its hidden inscriptions, which {{7}} like a built-in user's guide, and working reconstructions now turn at the twist of a hand crank. Historians of technology describe the find as humbling: it is a reminder that brilliance does not {{8}} in a straight line, and that whole crafts can vanish without a trace.

gaps.explanation: 'a lump of bronze that nobody could identify' — say what it was; intensify = make stronger, certify = confirm officially.
'it revealed gear wheels' — disclosed them; revise = change and improve, resent = feel bitter about.
'to predict the positions of the sun and moon' — calculate them in advance; the other pre- verbs share the form, not the meaning.
'mechanisms of this sophistication' — this level of refinement; sensation = a strong feeling or a scandal, saturation = the state of being full.
'was a lost tradition' — one that died out; lax = careless, and 'last' and 'least' reverse the meaning of the sentence.
'the skills were unrecorded — no manual survives' — never written down; unrehearsed = not practised, unrewarded = without a prize.
'inscriptions which read like a user's guide' — 'read like' = have the effect of; plead = beg, tread = step.
'brilliance does not progress in a straight line' — advance steadily; profess = claim, protrude = stick out.
